John 21
JON TWEN-tee-WUHN
proper noun
The twenty-first and final chapter of the Gospel of John; the risen Christ at the sea of Tiberias and the restoration of Peter.

Biblical Definition

John 21 is the closing chapter of the fourth Gospel, the risen Lord’s appearing to His disciples at the sea of Tiberias, the miraculous draught of fishes, and above all the tender restoration of Simon Peter. The disciples, having toiled all night and caught nothing, are told by the stranger on the shore to cast the net on the right side; the net is filled with a hundred fifty and three great fishes, and John knows that it is the Lord. After they have dined, the Lord turns to Peter, who had thrice denied Him, and asks three times, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me?—one searching question for each denial. Three times Peter affirms his love, grieved that he is asked the third time, and three times the Lord commissions him: Feed my lambs; feed my sheep; feed my sheep. The thrice-denying disciple is thrice restored and charged to shepherd the flock. The Lord then foretells the death by which Peter would glorify God and bids him simply, Follow me. When Peter asks about John, the Lord answers, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me. The Gospel closes confessing that the world itself could not contain the books of all that Jesus did. The dictionary reads John 21 as the gospel of restoring grace: the fallen disciple recommissioned by the love of Christ and sent to feed the sheep.

Webster 1828 Definition

The final chapter of John; the risen Christ at the sea of Tiberias, the great catch, and the threefold restoration of Peter—“Lovest thou me? Feed my sheep.”

Key Scripture

Joh 21:15 — "So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs."

Joh 21:17 — "He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep."

Joh 21:22 — "Jesus saith unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me."

Joh 21:25 — "And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen."

Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition, though Rome presses “feed my sheep” into a Petrine supremacy the text does not teach; rightly read, it is the restoration of a fallen disciple.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The misreading to answer is the Roman use of “Feed my sheep” to establish a Petrine supremacy and the papal office—as though Christ here made Peter the prince over the apostles and the church. But the threefold charge answers Peter’s threefold denial; it is restoration, not coronation. Peter is recommissioned to the common pastoral work all elders share—to feed the flock of God—not exalted to a monarchy over his brethren, who elsewhere stand as fellow-foundations and to whom the same keys are given. The chapter humbles Peter; it does not enthrone him.

The principle to recover is the restoring grace of Christ toward fallen disciples and the shepherd’s charge that flows from love to Him. The Lord does not cast off the disciple who denied Him but draws out his love and sends him to feed the sheep; the qualification for ministry is love to Christ, and the work is to feed His flock. And to Peter’s curiosity about another the Lord gives the word every disciple needs: what is that to thee? follow thou me.
